primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Out-of-frame dystrophin mutations cause absent dystrophin, progressive myofiber membrane instability, markedly elevated CK, calf pseudohypertrophy, and cardiomyopathy.
vignette: A 4-year-old boy has delayed motor milestones, frequent falls, calf pseudohypertrophy, and uses his hands to climb up his thighs when standing.
distractor_notes: Becker muscular dystrophy is generally milder and later onset due to partially functional dystrophin.
Spinal muscular atrophy causes lower motor neuron weakness without calf pseudohypertrophy.
Cerebral palsy is nonprogressive and usually has upper motor neuron signs.
Myasthenia causes fatigable weakness without marked CK elevation or pseudohypertrophy.
key_expl: Early childhood proximal weakness, Gowers sign, and calf pseudohypertrophy are classic Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: In-frame DMD mutations preserve the reading frame and produce reduced or abnormal dystrophin, yielding a milder later-onset phenotype than Duchenne disease.
vignette: A 16-year-old boy has slowly progressive proximal weakness and elevated CK but remains ambulatory. Genetic testing shows an in-frame deletion in DMD.
lead: Why is the phenotype milder than Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
correct: Some partially functional dystrophin is produced
distractors: The mutation increases dystrophin expression above normal
The disease affects only sensory nerves
The mutation prevents all muscle inflammation
The gene is autosomal rather than X-linked
distractor_notes: Becker mutations reduce or alter dystrophin rather than increase it.
The disorder affects muscle, not sensory nerves.
Muscle injury and degeneration still occur.
Both Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies are X-linked.
key_expl: Reading-frame preservation allows production of shortened but partially functional dystrophin in Becker muscular dystrophy.
objective: Explain the milder Becker phenotype through the reading-frame rule.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Becker disease as caused by dystrophin variants preserving partial protein function.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Interruption of blood supply to subchondral bone causes osteocyte death and structural collapse, associated with glucocorticoids, alcohol, trauma, and sickle cell disease.
vignette: A 48-year-old man on long-term high-dose glucocorticoids develops progressive groin pain worsened by weight bearing. MRI shows subchondral collapse of the femoral head.
correct: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head
distractor_notes: Osteoarthritis causes joint-space loss and osteophytes rather than focal subchondral bone death.
Septic arthritis usually causes acute severe pain and systemic inflammatory findings.
Osteomyelitis is bone infection.
Trochanteric bursitis causes lateral hip pain rather than groin pain and femoral-head collapse.
key_expl: Glucocorticoid exposure plus femoral-head subchondral collapse is classic avascular necrosis.
objective: Recognize avascular necrosis and its risk factors.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Giant cell tumor usually arises in the epiphysis of long bones after skeletal maturity and contains numerous osteoclast-like giant cells driven by RANKL-expressing stromal cells.
vignette: A 28-year-old woman has knee pain. Imaging shows an expansile lytic lesion extending to the articular surface of the distal femoral epiphysis.
lead: Which cell type accounts for the numerous multinucleated giant cells?
distractor_notes: Chondrocytes dominate cartilaginous tumors.
Neutrophils are inflammatory cells.
Plasma cells are not the characteristic giant-cell population.
Adipocytes are not multinucleated giant cells.
key_expl: The giant cells in giant cell tumor resemble osteoclasts and are recruited by neoplastic stromal cells.
objective: Identify osteoclast-like giant cells in giant cell tumor of bone.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: A lipoma is a benign neoplasm of mature adipocytes that typically presents as a soft, mobile, painless subcutaneous mass.
vignette: A 45-year-old man has a slowly growing, soft, mobile, painless subcutaneous mass on the shoulder.
lead: Which tissue is the neoplasm composed of?
distractor_notes: Skeletal-muscle tumors have a different clinical and histologic pattern.
Fibrocartilage is characteristic of cartilaginous lesions.
Nerve-sheath tumors arise from Schwann or related cells.
Vascular tumors derive from endothelial cells.
key_expl: Lipomas are benign tumors of mature adipocytes.
objective: Identify the tissue of origin of a lipoma.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Immune-mediated keratinocyte hyperproliferation produces sharply demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale, often on extensor surfaces and scalp.
vignette: A 35-year-old man has chronic sharply demarcated plaques with silvery scale on elbows and knees and pitting of the nails.
distractor_notes: Atopic dermatitis is intensely pruritic and often flexural.
Tinea corporis is annular with central clearing.
Seborrheic dermatitis affects greasy sebaceous areas.
Lichen planus causes violaceous polygonal pruritic papules.
key_expl: Extensor plaques with silvery scale and nail pitting are classic psoriasis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: T-cell-mediated injury to basal keratinocytes produces pruritic, purple, polygonal, planar papules and can involve oral mucosa.
vignette: A 50-year-old woman has intensely pruritic violaceous polygonal flat-topped papules on the wrists and white lacy oral lesions.
distractor_notes: IgE-mediated disease causes immediate allergy.
Desmoglein antibodies cause pemphigus vulgaris.
Glomerular immune complexes cause nephritis.
Oxidative burst failure causes CGD.
key_expl: Lichen planus is a lichenoid T-cell-mediated interface dermatitis.
objective: Explain the immune basis of lichen planus.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Autoimmune T-cell attack on anagen hair follicles causes sharply demarcated nonscarring hair loss.
vignette: A 24-year-old woman with autoimmune thyroid disease develops several smooth round patches of scalp hair loss without scarring.
distractors: Permanent destruction of follicles by fibrosis
Fungal invasion of hair shafts only
distractor_notes: Scarring alopecias destroy follicles permanently and leave scarred skin.
Androgenetic alopecia has patterned thinning, not sudden smooth patches.
Tinea capitis often has scale and broken hairs.
Melanocyte loss causes vitiligo.
key_expl: Alopecia areata is an autoimmune nonscarring alopecia affecting hair follicles.
objective: Recognize the autoimmune mechanism of alopecia areata.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Small chemicals act as haptens and trigger sensitized T-cell responses, causing delayed type IV hypersensitivity at exposed skin sites.
vignette: A woman develops a pruritic vesicular rash under a nickel bracelet 48 hours after wearing it.
distractor_notes: Type I reactions occur within minutes via IgE.
Type II reactions involve antibodies against cell or matrix antigens.
Type III reactions involve circulating immune complexes.
Complement deficiency does not cause localized delayed contact dermatitis.
key_expl: Allergic contact dermatitis is a T-cell-mediated delayed hypersensitivity reaction.
objective: Identify type IV hypersensitivity in allergic contact dermatitis.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: An acute immune-mediated reaction, often triggered by HSV or infection, produces symmetric targetoid lesions and limited mucosal involvement.
vignette: A 22-year-old man develops multiple symmetric target-shaped lesions on the hands and forearms several days after recurrent herpes labialis.
distractor_notes: SJS causes widespread epidermal necrosis with prominent mucosal involvement and systemic illness.
Urticaria causes transient wheals, not fixed target lesions.
Psoriasis causes scaly plaques.
Cellulitis causes localized warm erythema.
key_expl: Target lesions after HSV infection are classic erythema multiforme.
objective: Recognize erythema multiforme and distinguish it from SJS.
